a1.say: Let's build Streaming AI Chat UI.

a1.cap: Build a chat component that sends a question to /api/chat/stream?q=... (Server-Sent Events) and renders the answer token by token as it arrives, disables input while streaming, and closes the stream when done or destroyed.

lines: Build a chat component that sends a question to /api/chat/stream?q=... (Server-Sent Events) and renders the answer token by token as it arrives, disables input while streaming, and closes the stream when done or destroyed.

a1.cap: The browser's EventSource connects to an SSE endpoint and fires a handler per named event. Each token event appends text to an answer signal, so the view updates live. The done event, an error, or the component being destroyed closes the connection.
a1.say: The browser's Event Source connects to an SSE endpoint and fires a handler per named event. Each token event appends text to an answer signal, so the view updates live. The done event, an error, or the component being destroyed closes the connection.

a1.cap: This pairs with the Spring Boot SSE exercise to give an end-to-end streaming LLM feature.
Two-way binding keeps the question field in sync. It's disabled while an answer streams.
aria-live lets screen readers announce the growing answer.
The answer is a signal that grows token by token.
Close the connection if the user navigates away mid-answer.
EventSource opens the Server-Sent Events stream. Always URL-encode user input.
